front: In AWS Lambda, a job runs for most of an hour after each upload, with no servers to manage. Function or Fargate?
back: AWS Fargate. A function stops after 15 minutes per invocation.
extra: Fargate has [no hard limit on execution time](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-fargate-no-execution-time-limit).

front: In AWS Lambda, reserved or provisioned concurrency: which one removes cold starts?
back: Provisioned concurrency.
extra: A function with provisioned concurrency [does not exhibit cold start behavior](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-pc-not-latest-no-cold-start). Reserved concurrency sets capacity aside and caps it.

front: In AWS Lambda, a CPU-heavy function is slow. Which setting do you raise?
back: Memory. CPU grows in proportion to it.
extra: Lambda allocates CPU power [in proportion to the amount of memory](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-cpu-proportional-to-memory) configured.

front: In AWS Lambda, does Lambda retry a failed synchronous invocation by itself?
back: No. The caller retries.
extra: The caller can [view the error message in the response](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-sync-error-caller-retries) and [retry the invocation manually](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-sync-error-caller-retries).

front: In AWS Lambda, a function in a VPC must call an internet API. What does it need?
back: Private subnets with a route to a NAT gateway.
extra: A public subnet [doesn't give it internet access](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-vpc-public-subnet-no-internet). Private subnets [access the internet through the NAT gateway](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-vpc-public-subnet-no-internet).

front: In AWS Lambda, many concurrent functions exhaust the connections of an RDS database. What do you add?
back: Amazon RDS Proxy.
extra: Many environments can [exhaust database connection limits](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-vpc-db-connections-rds-proxy). RDS Proxy is there [to pool and manage connections](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-vpc-db-connections-rds-proxy).

front: In AWS Lambda, the maximum timeout of a function is {{c1::900 seconds}}.
extra: That is [15 minutes](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-timeout-max).

front: In AWS Lambda, the default timeout of a new function is {{c1::3 seconds}}.
extra: You adjust it in [increments of 1 second](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-timeout-default).

front: In AWS Lambda, a function's memory can be set from 128 MB to {{c1::10,240 MB}}.
extra: You change it in [1-MB increments](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-memory-range), and CPU follows it.

front: In AWS Lambda, the default concurrent executions quota per account per Region is {{c1::1,000}}.
extra: [Tens of thousands](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-concurrent-executions-default) is how high a quota increase can take it.

front: In AWS Lambda, after a failed asynchronous invocation, Lambda by default tries {{c1::two more times}}.
extra: The wait grows to [two minutes between the second and third attempts](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-async-default-two-retries).

front: In AWS Lambda, a synchronous request payload can be at most {{c1::6 MB}}.
extra: The response of a synchronous call has the same limit.

front: In AWS Lambda, a container image function can be up to {{c1::10 GB}} uncompressed.
extra: The size includes all layers of the image.

front: In AWS Lambda, the /tmp storage of a function can be set from 512 MB to {{c1::10,240 MB}}.
extra: You change it in [1-MB increments](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-tmp-storage-range).

front: In AWS Lambda, can a Service Quotas request raise the maximum function timeout?
back: No. Function configuration quotas cannot be changed.
extra: For the configuration quotas, the quotas page says: [Except as noted, they can't be changed](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-config-quotas-not-changeable).

front: In AWS Lambda with an SQS event source, where do the messages that keep failing go?
back: To the source queue's dead-letter queue, through its redrive policy.
extra: The [visibility timeout and redrive policy](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-queue-esm-retry-set-on-queue) are set [on the source queue](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-queue-esm-retry-set-on-queue).

front: In AWS Lambda with an SQS event source, how long should the queue's visibility timeout be?
back: At least six times the function timeout.
extra: Set the [visibility timeout](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-sqs-visibility-six-times-timeout) to [at least six times](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-sqs-visibility-six-times-timeout) the function timeout, so Lambda has time to retry after throttling.

front: In AWS Lambda, a standby Region must take the full load after a failover. Which quota do you raise there?
back: That Region's concurrency quota, ahead of time.
extra: Quotas for concurrent executions apply [per AWS Region](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-quota-scope-region-vs-vpc).

front: In AWS Lambda, can you configure provisioned concurrency on $LATEST?
back: No. Only on a published version or an alias.
extra: It must be applied to [a specific version or alias of a function](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-pc-not-latest-no-cold-start), [not the $LATEST version](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-pc-not-latest-no-cold-start).

front: In AWS Lambda, SnapStart or provisioned concurrency: which one fits a strict double-digit millisecond startup?
back: Provisioned concurrency. SnapStart is best effort.
extra: SnapStart is a [best-effort optimization](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-faq-snapstart-vs-pc). For [double-digit millisecond](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-faq-snapstart-vs-pc) startup times, AWS recommends provisioned concurrency.

front: In AWS Lambda, partners need their own API keys and usage plans. Function URL or API Gateway?
back: Amazon API Gateway.
extra: [API keys for usage plans](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-apigw-extra-features-waf-keys) are a feature that API Gateway adds and function URLs lack.

front: In AWS Lambda, which kind of Savings Plan lowers the cost of functions?
back: A Compute Savings Plan.
extra: [Compute Savings Plans](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-sp-ec2-instance-plans-exclude-lambda) apply to Lambda usage. EC2 Instance Savings Plans and Reserved Instances do not.

front: In AWS Lambda, where does data go that must survive between invocations?
back: A durable store, such as DynamoDB or Amazon S3.
extra: Assume that the environment [exists only for a single invocation](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-stateless-store-state-elsewhere).

front: In AWS Lambda, how do you stop a runaway function at once without deleting it?
back: Set its reserved concurrency to 0.
extra: AWS advises to [set the function reserved concurrency to 0](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-bp-runaway-reserved-zero), which will [throttle all invocations to the function](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-bp-runaway-reserved-zero).

front: In AWS Lambda, an event source mapping can deliver one record twice. How must the code behave?
back: Idempotently: a repeated record changes nothing.
extra: Event source mappings [process each event at least once](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-esm-at-least-once).

front: In AWS Lambda, can an S3 bucket be the on-success destination of asynchronous invocations?
back: No. An S3 bucket serves on failure only.
extra: [S3 buckets are supported only for on-failure destinations](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-async-s3-destination-on-failure-only).

front: In AWS Lambda with an SQS event source, how do you retry only the failed messages of a batch?
back: A partial batch response, with ReportBatchItemFailures.
extra: The event source mapping can then [make only the failed messages visible again](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-sqs-partial-batch-response).

front: In AWS Lambda with a Kinesis stream, one bad record blocks a shard. Which setting splits the failed batch?
back: BisectBatchOnFunctionError.
extra: It [splits a failed batch into two smaller batches](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-stream-bisect-batch-on-error) and isolates the bad records.

front: In AWS Lambda, trigger or event source mapping: which one is a resource of the Lambda service?
back: The event source mapping.
extra: A trigger is [stored and managed by the service](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-trigger-stored-by-source-esm-in-lambda) that generates the events.

front: In AWS Lambda, Amazon S3 must invoke a function. Which policy must allow it?
back: The function's resource-based policy.
extra: When an AWS service calls the function, [Lambda considers only the resource-based policy](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-service-caller-resource-policy-only).

front: In AWS Lambda, how do you send a small share of traffic to a new version?
back: A weighted alias, as a canary release.
extra: You test the new version with a [small percentage of traffic](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-weighted-alias-canary) and can [quickly roll back](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-weighted-alias-canary).

front: In AWS Lambda, where does AWS recommend keeping database credentials?
back: AWS Secrets Manager, not environment variables.
extra: AWS recommends that you [use AWS Secrets Manager instead of environment variables](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-secrets-manager-not-env-vars).
